assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational account of how collateral and balance sheets amplify macroeconomic fluctuations, with exceptional influence on macro-finance.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supplied the seminal collateral-constraint mechanism; Gertler is central to the financial-accelerator formulation.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms have been extensively developed, quantified and applied, especially since the global financial crisis.
uncertainties: The full intellectual lineage and appropriate three-person allocation remain contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework transformed modern monetary theory and policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Calvo pricing, Taylor rules and Woodford's synthesis are each indispensable elements, though the candidate encompasses many major contributors.
assessment.maturity: This is a decades-old framework with pervasive use in central-bank research and macroeconomic policy evaluation.
uncertainties: A three-person prize cannot fully represent the broad set of foundational contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection provided a highly influential new basis for analyzing trade, productivity and welfare.
assessment.attribution: Melitz's model is the pivotal contribution, while Helpman and Redding made major related theoretical and empirical advances.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated a large, durable literature and shaped empirical trade research.
uncertainties: The relative boundary between the core model and its subsequent extensions requires careful attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods made credible estimation feasible for a broad class of economic applications.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond supplied the canonical estimator, with Blundell central to the system-GMM extension.
assessment.maturity: The methods are long established and exceptionally widely used across applied economics.
uncertainties: Widespread mechanical application and finite-sample limitations complicate assessment of the contribution's ultimate empirical legacy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile methods fundamentally expanded econometric analysis beyond conditional means and enabled modern distributional work.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett originated quantile regression; Chernozhukov made major advances in high-dimensional and structural distributional methods.
assessment.maturity: The original method is mature and has found enduring use across econometrics and applied work.
uncertainties: Chernozhukov's relation to the original core contribution is less direct than that of the originators.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work gave political economy a rigorous, broadly applicable account of how institutions and incentives shape fiscal policy and development.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini established central models of political institutions, while Besley made defining contributions on accountability and state capacity.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda is long-standing, theoretically coherent and deeply integrated into public and development economics.
uncertainties: The candidate aggregates several related institutional literatures rather than a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research provided influential evidence and frameworks for understanding technological and trade-driven changes in jobs and wage inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are central to the task and local-labor-market analyses, with Katz important to the broader inequality literature.
assessment.maturity: Its findings have been tested extensively and remain central to research and policy debates.
uncertainties: Separating causal effects of trade, technology and other concurrent labor-market changes remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and sharpened understanding of place, policy and opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are core architects of the research program, while Katz is an important collaborator in parts of it.
assessment.maturity: The measurement infrastructure and major findings have already reshaped public-economics research, though the agenda remains active.
uncertainties: The comparatively recent evidence base leaves open how durable particular causal interpretations will prove.
